meta.description: Call number parity corpus. Every composer (library-metadata-lookup LibraryItem.call_number, Backend-Service computeCallNumber, dj-site libraryCode.ts) drives its tests from these rows so the three cannot drift apart by hand. Canonical JSON: src/test-utils/call-number-cases.json; non-TS consumers vendor it from the published tarball and pin its SHA-256.

schema.id: Unique kebab-case identifier for the row (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens).
schema.why: One line: what the row pins.
schema.genre: Genre name, or null. dj-site branches on numeric genre_id: map Rock to 11, Soundtracks to 12, any other name to any other id, and null to undefined.
schema.format: Format word (cd, CD, LP, ...), verbatim, or null.
schema.call_letters: Artist code letters as stored, verbatim (V/A, Z-M, ST, ...), or null.
schema.volume_letters: Per-release volume letters, or null. No composer renders them yet (LML#1373, Backend-Service#2827); seeded null.
schema.comp_letter: Compilation bin letter as a first-class input, or null. No composer reads it yet (LML#1431, Backend-Service#2837, dj-site#1791). A row with comp_letter null and a bin only on artist_name pins the TARGET that the name is ignored, so LML and Backend carry pending until they delete their name-reading.
schema.artist_name: Artist name as stored, or null. Kept only so a row can pin that the name is ignored once name-reading is deleted.
schema.full: The LML/Backend string: <Genre> <Format> <artist half><release half>, where the artist half drops dj-site's trailing '/' or '-' when there is no release number. Empty only when the row has nothing to compose.
schema.artist_half: What dj-site formatArtistCodeWithPunctuation returns (trailing punctuation included), or null when the row has no artist half dj-site would render.
schema.release_half: What dj-site formatReleaseCode returns, or null when the row has no release number.
schema.pending: Optional object keyed by consumer (lml, backend, djsite) whose value is an OPEN ticket ref (owner/repo#N) whose acceptance criteria close that consumer's divergence from the row's target. A consumer that already matches carries no marker. That consumer skips or expects-fail the row until the ticket lands. Never this corpus's own issue.

decisions.decision: Partial rows render LML#1432's form: letters with no artist number is "Rock cd ST/3", no artist half is "Rock cd 3", a release number alone is "3".
decisions.rationale: Decided 2026-10-05. Backend-Service#2827 aligns computeCallNumber; until then the three partial rows carry pending.backend. Backend's rows always have an artist number today (library_artist_view INNER JOINs genre_artist_crossreference and artist_genre_code is NOT NULL), so its side is latent.

decisions.decision: Letter case is undecided: LML and Backend render call_letters verbatim, dj-site upper-cases it.
decisions.rationale: No source produces lowercase call letters today, so the corpus seeds uppercase rows only and carries no lowercase-input row that depends on the rule; it is left to whichever ticket decides it.

decisions.decision: A compilation bin that exists only in the artist name renders the no-letter form: names are ignored. The bin letter is read only from comp_letter (or the legacy Z-<letter> code).
decisions.rationale: Epic Backend-Service#2828 deletes name-reading. LML and Backend read the name today (pending LML#1431, Backend-Service#2837); dj-site already ignores it. artist_name stays an input only to pin that the name is ignored.

cases.why: The regular named-artist shape.
No release number drops the release half; dj-site always has one, so it asserts no release half.
A row with only a genre composes to the genre.
A row with only a format composes to the format.
A row with no inputs composes to the empty string.
A missing format is skipped, not rendered as a blank.
Partial row, decided 2026-10-05 (LML#1432): only a release number renders as the bare number. Backend drops the whole row (""); its rows always have an artist number today, so that side is latent.
Partial row, decided 2026-10-05 (LML#1432): no artist half renders the release alone. Backend drops the release; its rows always have an artist number today, so that side is latent.
Partial row, decided 2026-10-05 (LML#1432): letters with no artist number render Letters/Release. Backend renders the letters alone.
A named artist is untouched by the compilation branch (LML table).
A named artist with a two-digit artist number is untouched by the compilation branch (Backend table).
A V/A compilation in a single-bin genre files by title: V/A-Release, never V/A 0/Release.

A Rock compilation whose bin exists only as a trailing " - <letter>" on the artist name renders the no-letter form: the name is ignored. LML and Backend still read it from the name until their name-reading is deleted; dj-site already ignores names.
The Rock bin letter supplied structurally as comp_letter, with no name to read, renders V/A <L>-Release. No composer reads comp_letter yet.
A Soundtracks compilation whose bin exists only on the artist name renders the no-letter form V/A-Release: the name is ignored. LML and Backend still read it until their name-reading is deleted.
The Soundtracks bin letter supplied as comp_letter renders the bare letter with no V/A word. No composer reads comp_letter yet.
Soundtracks with no recoverable bin falls back to V/A-Release.
V/A is recognized structurally, case- and whitespace-insensitively.
The legacy Z-<letter> spelling carries its bin at index 2 of the code; the name is deliberately unrelated to prove it is not read.
Legacy Z-<letter> on Soundtracks renders the bare bin.
Legacy Z-- is a compilation with no bin.
Legacy Z-M on a single-bin genre drops the bin (the Java renders it only for Rock and Soundtracks).
Legacy Z- takes any non-hyphen character at index 2, as substring(2, 3) does.
A Rock bin heading on the name is ignored under a non-Rock genre.
A trailing " - <letter>" on the name is ignored outside Rock and Soundtracks.
A multi-letter name suffix is not a bin letter.
A multi-letter Rock heading suffix is not a bin letter.
The name is trimmed at both ends before the bin suffix is read, so " - M" alone is not a bin.
A null release number on a compilation drops the release half and its hyphen.
A null release number on a Rock compilation whose bin exists only on the artist name renders bare V/A: the name is ignored. LML and Backend still read it until their name-reading is deleted.
A null release number on a Rock compilation with comp_letter keeps the bin and drops the trailing hyphen. No composer reads comp_letter yet.
Null genre and format are skipped, leaving the bare locator; with no genre there is no bin (LML table).
Null genre and format are skipped, leaving the bare locator (Backend table).
